title: Redwood PLG Quickstart Discovery - Nova Edge (Follow)
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 17:34 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording: auto
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Nova Edge), Alison Rivera, Priya Singh

Summary: Intro to Redwood PLG quickstart, focus on time-to-first-token for devs, discuss free PLG credits and a path to a Dedicated pilot for high-volume workloads. Security questions (SOC2, SSO, KMS) surfaced and next steps agreed for a benchmark kickoff.

Topics: Quickstart onboarding; Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; Time-to-first-token expectations; Security/compliance; Benchmarking pilot and pricing.

00:00 Jordan: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood inference, i lead accounts in this region
00:06 Samir: hi jordan, i'm samir, head of ml at nova edge. we run an embeddings search service and want to reduce infra lift by using hosted apis for fast feature rollout
00:18 Jordan: awesome, priya our se is with me and she'll walk through the quickstart and the benchmarking approach
00:26 Priya: hey all, quick question before i demo, what are your top success metrics for this project?
00:33 Alison: p99 latency under 200ms for user facing chat, cost per 1k tokens needs to be sustainable, and a fast path to first token in devideally under an hour
00:49 Jordan: perfect, our PLG quickstart is built for that; most devs get first token in 10-30 minutes once they can reach the console
01:02 Samir: what's the main tradeoff between hosted and dedicated for us? we have some data residency requirements too
01:11 Priya: hosted is fastest to onboard and pay-as-you-go; dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation; private is for VPC/on-prem with customer-managed networking and KMS.
01:28 Alison: is dedicated truly isolated from other tenants?
01:33 Priya: yes, dedicated is your own pool, isolated compute and stronger data controls; hosted also supports enterprise controls like audit logs and SSO if that fits your risk profile
01:45 Samir: we'd like to PLG on hosted and then pilot dedicated for the high qps search path. is that a usual flow?
01:53 Jordan: very typical. start on hosted, validate, then move to dedicated when you need sustained throughput or strict isolation.
02:05 Priya: i'll walkthrough the quickstart steps: signup, create api key in console, run curl or SDK sample, call text-generation or embeddings endpoint; node/python samples included
02:19 Alison: we have corp proxy/egress filtering. any special steps?
02:27 Priya: if egress is blocked you can either open allowlist to redwood endpoints or use private deployment; we also provide a proxy-friendly example in the quickstart repo
02:41 Samir: what about credits — what do you typically offer?
02:45 Jordan: standard PLG credits range; for pilots we often provide $5k credits and a short support window for benchmark assistance. credits apply to hosted usage.
02:58 Priya: note that credits are on hosted accounts; for dedicated benchmarks we help run a short side-by-side perf test to compare unit economics and latency.
03:11 Priya: time-to-first-token can be sub-hour if SSO and network are straightforward; recommend one dev as owner and we provide a small onboarding runbook
03:25 Alison: security: our infosec asks for SOC2, SAML, audit logs, and KMS options. do you have SOC2?
03:34 Jordan: yes, SOC2 type II available and we'll attach the security pack. we support SAML/SSO and RBAC; dedicated/private support customer KMS/HSM integrations.
03:47 Priya: for private we can ship audit logs to your SIEM and support extended retention as an add-on
03:56 Priya Singh: question, can we bring our own kms in Dedicated? we require customer key separation
04:02 Priya: yes, both Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS; for on-prem we can integrate with your HSM vendor.
04:13 Samir: on latency vs cost, we have high qps for embeddings and we want to optimize without hurting p99 for chat
04:22 Priya: levers include batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles; for embeddings high batch sizes are efficient, for chat we tune instance sizing and batch behavior to keep p99 low. we will optimize after the benchmark.
04:36 Alison: can we pin models to avoid accidental upgrades?
04:40 Priya: yes, model pinning and canary rollouts are supported; automatic fallback to compatible variants is available.
04:49 Samir: gotchas in the quickstart examples for node? we use node heavily
04:54 Priya: node/python examples exist; common gotcha is env var names and proxies. we'll include a node proxy sample in the quickstart bundle.
05:06 Jordan: pricing for Dedicated pilot — any ballpark for 1-2 reserved gpus?
05:13 Priya: varies by GPU family; we'll propose a pilot estimate (reserved monthly base + burst usage). we'll include ballpark numbers in follow up.
05:27 Samir: timeline — we'd like to start infra tests in two weeks and run a pilot in Q2
05:34 Jordan: we can align credits and a benchmark window to hit that timeline
05:42 Priya: minor note: transcription sometimes mangles terms (e.g., 'KV cache' becomes 'k v cash'), so watch docs for that
05:51 Alison: ha yes we've seen that in transcripts
05:56 Priya Singh: data residency — do you support EU-only hosting?
06:01 Jordan: yes, hosted region routing to eu-west is available; Dedicated/private can be deployed in customer-preferred regions or on-prem.
06:14 Samir: what's the next step to get devs started on hosted and plan a Dedicated benchmark?
06:21 Jordan: immediate — send quickstart link + node sample + one-time credits; short term — schedule 60m benchmark kickoff with our se; mid-term — scoping doc for Dedicated pilot.
06:37 Alison: competitors we looked at: OpenAI for hosted simplicity and cloud providers or inference specialists for dedicated
06:44 Jordan: commonly mentioned competitors: OpenAI, Anthropic, Vertex AI, SageMaker
06:54 Samir: any migration friction from hosted to dedicated?
07:00 Priya: we keep the same API and model catalog; main work is network config and tuning for instance types. our team assists with migration.
07:15 Samir: can you share a sample benchmark report to vet methodology with infra?
07:21 Priya: yes, we'll attach a sample benchmark report and runbook.
07:29 Jordan: recap owners
07:33 Jordan: jordan to send quickstart + credits + security pack by 2026-03-06
07:38 Priya: priya to scope benchmark and prepare node sample by 2026-03-11
07:46 Alison: alison to share latency targets and sample traces by 2026-03-08
07:51 Samir: samir to introduce infra lead on email thread by 2026-03-05
07:57 Jordan: any final Qs?
08:01 Alison: none, thanks

(transcription notes: medium quality, occasional mis-hearings and filler words, e.g., 'kv cache' miswritten)
